# Renting in a big city for the first time: what should you confirm before signing? {#first-rent}

It comes down to three things: **confirm the person, the flat and the money**. Verify the landlord's identity and ownership, write the key terms into the contract, and keep evidence of every payment and the handover.

- Check the landlord's identity and ownership before signing; do not rely on verbal promises.
- Rent, deposit, term, penalties and repair duties must be in the contract.
- Pay in a way that leaves a record, and inspect and photograph every item at handover.

@answer scope="Cities in mainland China · whole or shared flat in an ordinary home · first lease"
@meta locale=en

## In what order do you check before signing? {#flow}

@workflow id=rent-flow title="Checks before signing"
| lane verify | Verify |
| lane paper | Contract and money |
| lane move | Handover |
| see | View the flat | external | verify |
| id | Check identity and ownership | backend | verify |
| ok | Signer verified? | backend | verify |
| walk | Walk away | external | verify |
| terms | Write terms into the contract | backend | paper |
| pay | Pay and keep receipts | backend | paper |
| check | Inspect and photograph | backend | move |
| see > id | |
| id > ok | |
| ok > walk | No | dashed |
| ok > terms | Yes | emphasis |
| terms > pay | |
| pay > check | |

@steps id=rent-steps
| see | View the flat | Visit once in the evening and once at the weekend; test light, noise, water pressure and phone signal; check the commute. | rent-flow | see |
| id | Check identity and ownership | See the original ID card and the property certificate; confirm the signer is the owner, or an agent with the owner's power of attorney. | rent-flow | id |
| terms | Write terms into the contract | To avoid disputes, put the key promises into the contract or an addendum, confirmed by both sides. | rent-flow | terms |
| pay | Pay and keep receipts | Note the purpose on each transfer; ask for a receipt, or have the contract state the amount received. | rent-flow | pay |
| check | Inspect and photograph | Photograph the water, power and gas meter readings, the furniture and appliances, and any existing damage. | rent-flow | check |

## Which terms must the contract spell out? {#clauses}

| Term | What to confirm | Common trap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rent and payment | Amount, payment cycle, the receiving account is the landlord's own | The payee is not the landlord {bad:High risk} |
| Deposit | Amount, conditions and deadline for its return | Deductions as "cleaning" or "wear" fees {bad:High risk} |
| Term and move-out | Start and end dates, penalty for leaving early | The whole deposit kept as a penalty {caution:Watch} |
| Repairs | Who fixes and pays for appliances, pipes and wiring | Everything pushed onto the tenant {caution:Watch} |
| Subletting and renewal | Whether you may sublet, how much rent may rise on renewal | No subletting and no early exit either {caution:Watch} |
| Utilities and fees | Who pays water, power, gas, management, internet and heating | The previous tenant's arrears billed to you {caution:Watch} |

## What do you check on signing day? {#day-of}

@facts id=day-checks
| Landlord's ID card | Check the original; the name matches the property certificate |
| Property certificate | Check the address and the owner |
| Signing through an agent | Requires a power of attorney signed by the owner |
| First payment | Deposit plus the first rent period, amount written into the contract |
| Agency fee | Often half a month to a month's rent; agree it in advance (rule of thumb) |

@callout level=warning title="Walk away if you see these"
| Photos only, no viewing allowed, and pressure to pay a holding fee first.
| No proof of ownership, or a sublessor without the owner's written consent to sublet.
| Cash or a transfer to a third party's account demanded, with no receipt.
| A newly renovated flat with a sharp smell, or an obvious partitioned or overcrowded unit.

## What do you check at handover? {#handover}

- [ ] Write down the water, power and gas meter readings and photograph them
- [ ] Test the air conditioner, water heater, gas stove, washing machine and toilet drain
- [ ] Check door and window locks, water pressure and leaks
- [ ] Record existing damage to walls and floors, and send the photos to the landlord
- [ ] Count the keys and access cards
- [ ] Confirm the previous tenant's water, power, gas and management fees are settled

# P99 rose from 80 ms to 600 ms while the mean barely moved: a few requests got slow {#p99-tail}

A P99 spike with a flat mean means the slowest 1–2% of requests went from 80 ms to 600 ms while the rest stayed normal. The usual causes are queueing and contention, one bad instance or a slow downstream, or a few requests taking a slow path. Start the triage from the traces of slow requests, not from global metrics.

- The mean is blind to the tail: 15 of 1000 requests at 600 ms raise the mean by only about 8 ms.
- A worse tail almost always means one subset of requests has a problem, not the whole endpoint.
- The order: first find which segment is slow, then slice by dimension, then compare with changes and resources.

@answer scope="Illustrative numbers · a typical web or microservice endpoint · P99 is the 990th of 1000 values"
@meta locale=en

## Why did the mean not move? {#why-mean-flat}

```mermaid title="Endpoint latency before and after"
xychart-beta
  x-axis ["Mean", "P50", "P99"]
  y-axis "ms" 0 --> 700
  bar "Before" [80, 80, 80]
  bar "After" [88, 80, 600]
```

Take 985 requests at 80 ms plus 15 at 600 ms. The mean is `(985×80 + 15×600) / 1000 = 87.8` ms, only 7.8 ms more. P99 takes the 990th value, which falls among the 15 slow requests, so it jumps to 600 ms. The mean hides tail problems, which is exactly why you monitor P95 and P99.

## In what order do you triage? {#triage-order}

@workflow id=p99-triage title="Triage order: locate first, then slice"
| lane locate | Locate |
| lane split | Slice |
| lane fix | Compare |
| confirm | Confirm the metric | external | locate |
| trace | Sample slow traces | backend | locate |
| dim | Slice by instance, downstream, parameter | backend | split |
| change | Compare releases and config | backend | fix |
| res | Check resource contention | backend | fix |
| confirm > trace | Real |
| trace > dim | Slow segment |
| dim > change | One dimension |
| change > res | No change |

@steps id=triage-steps
| s1 | Confirm the metric | Check whether P50 and P95 rose too, and rule out a change in aggregation or sampling. | p99-triage | confirm |
| s2 | Sample slow traces | Pull at least 10 traces of 500 ms or more; see whether the time goes to queueing, downstream calls or own processing. | p99-triage | trace |
| s3 | Slice by instance, downstream, parameter | Are the slow requests on one instance, one downstream, or do they share a parameter? | p99-triage | dim |
| s4 | Compare releases and config | Line the spike's start up with deploys, config changes, feature flags and dependency upgrades. | p99-triage | change |
| s5 | Check resource contention | Look at connection pool waits, thread pool queues, GC pauses, CPU throttling and lock contention. | p99-triage | res |

## What are the likely causes? {#causes}

| Candidate cause | Typical sign | How to confirm |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Queueing and contention | Waiting dominates the trace; latency moves with load | Check connection and thread pool wait times and queue depth {caution:Most common} |
| One bad instance | Slow requests sit on one or two nodes | Slice P99 by instance and find the outlier |
| Slow downstream tail | Downstream spans take over 80% of slow traces | Check slow queries, lock waits and cache hit rate |
| Slow path or unusual parameters | Slow requests share a parameter, a user or a large body | Cluster the features of the slow samples |
| GC or runtime pauses | Periodic spikes that line up with the GC log | Compare stop-the-world pauses with the spike times |
| Retry amplification | Occasional downstream timeouts trigger retries | Check whether downstream QPS rose in step |

## Checklist {#checklist}

- [ ] Pull the last hour's traces of 500 ms or more, at least 10
- [ ] Slice the slow requests by instance, downstream and endpoint parameter
- [ ] Line the spike's start up with the deploy, config and flag timeline
- [ ] Check pool waits, GC pauses and CPU throttling metrics
- [ ] Confirm the P50 and P95 trend, to tell a worse tail from a metric change

# What happens when a browser opens an HTTPS site for the first time? {#first-visit}

The browser resolves the hostname, opens TCP, then runs a **one-round-trip TLS 1.3 handshake**. It agrees fresh encryption keys and checks the server's identity before any request is sent.

- The browser sends its key share inside `ClientHello`, so one round trip is enough.[](source:rfc8446)
- After `ServerHello` everything is encrypted, including the server's certificate.[](source:rfc8446)
- `CertificateVerify` proves the server holds the certificate's private key.
- Keys come from ephemeral shares, so a later leak of the private key cannot decrypt this session.

@answer scope="TLS 1.3 over TCP · first visit to a host · no proxy, no resumption"
@meta locale=en
@source rfc8446 title="RFC 8446: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3" url=https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446

## What crosses the wire before the first request? {#wire}

@sequence id=tls-visit title="First HTTPS visit: DNS to first response"
| actor browser | Browser | frontend |
| actor dns | DNS resolver | external |
| actor server | Web server | backend |
| phase | Name lookup |
| browser | dns | DNS query: example.com |
| dns | browser | IP address | return |
| phase | TCP handshake · 1 RTT |
| browser | server | SYN |
| server | browser | SYN + ACK | return |
| browser | server | ACK |
| phase | TLS 1.3 handshake · 1 RTT |
| browser | server | ClientHello: suites, SNI, key share |
| server | browser | ServerHello: chosen suite, key share | return |
| server | browser | Certificate + CertificateVerify + Finished, encrypted | return |
| browser | server | Finished | emphasis |
| phase | Encrypted HTTP |
| browser | server | GET / |
| server | browser | 200 OK + page | return |

@steps id=visit-steps
| resolve | DNS resolver | Turns the hostname into an IP before the connection can start. | tls-visit | dns |
| hello | Browser | Opens TCP and sends `ClientHello` with TLS 1.3, cipher suites, the hostname and an ephemeral key share. | tls-visit | browser |
| prove | Web server | Sends its key share, then certificate and `Finished` under encryption; checks the client's `Finished`. | tls-visit | server |

@callout id=quic level=note title="What about HTTP/3?"
| With QUIC, the TCP steps disappear: QUIC runs the same TLS 1.3 handshake inside the transport, still in one round trip.

## How does the browser know this is the real site? {#trust}

| Check | What the browser verifies |
| --- | --- |
| Chain | The certificate chains to a root CA in the browser's trust store. |
| Hostname | The site's name appears in the certificate's subject alternative name (SAN) list. |
| Validity | Today sits inside the certificate's not-before and not-after dates. |
| Ownership | `CertificateVerify` signs the handshake transcript; only the private-key holder could produce it. |
| Revocation | Stapled OCSP or CRLs, checked best-effort; many browsers accept an unreachable check. {caution:Weak} |

## Where do the session keys come from? {#keys}

@facts id=key-facts
| Key shares | Each side sends an ephemeral Diffie-Hellman share, usually X25519. |
| Shared secret | Each side combines its private share with the peer's public share. |
| Key schedule | HKDF expands the secret plus the transcript into handshake, then traffic keys. |
| Forward secrecy | Shares are discarded after use, so later key theft cannot decrypt this session. |
| Client `Finished` | Confirms both sides hold the same keys; the request can now ride on them. |

## What changes on the next visit? {#revisit}

| Aspect | First visit | Resumed visit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server proof | Full certificate and signature check | Pre-shared key from a `NewSessionTicket` |
| Round trips to first byte | DNS + TCP + 1 RTT of TLS | TCP, then data can ride with `ClientHello` {good:0-RTT} |
| Early data risk | None; the request waits for `Finished` | 0-RTT data can be replayed, so servers limit what it may do {caution:Replayable} |

# Which modules does Archify finalize go through, and how is the old artifact kept safe on failure? {#finalize-modules}

`finalize` is an orchestrator, not a renderer. `runFinalize` calls the three subcommands `deliver → check → browser-check` in order (validate runs inside deliver). Each gate uses sha256 and `receiptId` to confirm its receipt is bound to this artifact. The first failure stops the run. The old artifact is replaced only at deliver's commit point. The new HTML is first rendered and checked in a `.archify-delivery-*` staging area in the same directory. At commit the old file is backed up, then the new one is swapped in with a hard link. A failure midway rolls back automatically. If even the rollback fails, the recovery directory is kept.

- All three gates reuse the same CLI; finalize checks each receipt's type, byte count and hash.[](source:finalize-mjs)
- Nothing is written to the target path before commit; at commit it backs up first, then `linkSync`, and aborts on any binding mismatch.[](source:commit)
- The delivery lock and the pending journal make an interruption fail closed: concurrent runs are refused, leftover state is not trusted.[](source:deliver)
- Limit: a check or browser-check failure after a successful commit does not roll back; the old artifact is kept only up to the commit point.

@answer scope="Archify @ 82c47ca · bin/finalize.mjs + archify.mjs · explainer has no browser-check gate by default"
@meta locale=en repo_url=https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify repo_revision=82c47ca31d83749020ff30d6b1172248e71d255d
@source finalize-mjs title="runFinalize orchestrator" path=archify/bin/finalize.mjs lines=722:1050
@source commit title="commitDeliveryPair: backup, commit, rollback" path=archify/bin/archify.mjs lines=3236:3624
@source deliver title="commandDeliver main delivery flow" path=archify/bin/archify.mjs lines=4400:5301
@source check-cmd title="check and provenance checks" path=archify/bin/archify.mjs lines=5418:5659
@source recover title="recover-output.mjs recovery entry" path=archify/bin/recover-output.mjs lines=1:41

## Which gates does finalize split a delivery into? {#gates}

An explainer candidate is first compiled by `prepareExplainerInput` into a frozen bundle, and before and after each gate its dependencies are rechecked as unchanged. Native diagrams run all three gates by default; an explainer runs only `deliver + check`, and the browser gate opens only with `--browser-check`.

@workflow id=finalize-gates title="The finalize module chain"
| lane orch | Orchestrate bin/finalize.mjs |
| lane del | Deliver subcommand |
| lane ver | Verify subcommands |
| cli | commandFinalize parses args | backend | orch |
| snap | Snapshot candidate, open receipt | backend | orch |
| del | Lock, journal, staged render | backend | del |
| commit | commitDeliveryPair | backend | del |
| chk | check strict recheck | backend | ver |
| brw | browser-check Chrome | backend | ver |
| rec | .finalize.json receipt | database | orch |
| cli > snap | |
| snap > del | |
| del > commit | |
| commit > chk | pass |
| chk > brw | pass |
| brw > rec | |

@steps id=gate-steps
| parse | commandFinalize parses args | Parses quality, repo and out-dir; precompiles an explainer into a frozen bundle; starts a bounded update check in parallel. | finalize-gates | cli |
| snap | Snapshot candidate, open receipt | Records the input sha256; both receipt paths are captured atomically before writing. | finalize-gates | snap |
| del | Lock, journal, staged render | Takes the delivery lock and writes the pending journal; rendering and self-checks run in staging; any failing gate stops the run and writes diagnostics. | finalize-gates | del |
| chk | check strict recheck | Runs the strict checks once provenance=current and the sha matches, then the browser gate. | finalize-gates | chk |

## Which step fails, and what state is the old artifact in? {#failure-matrix}

| Failure point | Old artifact at the output path | Protection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Arguments, input or validate fail | Untouched {good:Safe} | Nothing touches the target before rendering; the delivery lock is not taken yet |
| Staged render or deliver's artifact check fails | Untouched {good:Safe} | The candidate is written only to `.archify-delivery-*`; a failed check reports previous artifact was preserved |
| `commitDeliveryPair` fails midway | Rolled back {good:Safe} | The old files are first backed up as `.previous-output` and `.previous-provenance`; on error each is linked back and its binding rechecked |
| Rollback fails or the lock is lost | Left in the recovery directory {caution:Manual} | `recoveryRequired`: the staging directory is kept, and `recover-output.mjs` can restore the old files |
| Another deliver runs, or a lock/pending is left over | Blocked by the lock {good:Safe} | `delivery/concurrent-attempt` or `lock-stale`; the new delivery refuses to start |
| check or browser-check fails after deliver committed | Already replaced by the new artifact {caution:Limit} | The new artifact passed its own checks; finalize reports fail and writes diagnostics, no automatic revert |

## Which files does a finalize leave on disk? {#sidecars}

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `<out>.delivery.json` | Success provenance: `receiptId`, the spec and artifact sha256, validation summary |
| `<out>.delivery-pending.json` | In-progress journal; deleted at commit, a leftover is evidence of an interrupted delivery |
| `<out>.delivery-lock.json` | Delivery lock; blocks concurrent and stale deliveries |
| `<out>.browser-check.json` | Browser evidence receipt; produced by default for native diagrams |
| `<out>.finalize.json` and `-summary.json` | Full and compact finalize receipts, published atomically through a temp file plus binding |
| `.archify-delivery-*` directory | Staging: spec snapshot, render candidate, `.previous-*` backups; cleaned up normally, kept when recovery is needed |

## After an interrupted delivery, in what order do you check? {#recovery}

- [ ] Read `failedStage` and `diagnostics[].supportedFixes` in `.finalize-summary.json` to see which gate stopped it.
- [ ] On `recoveryRequired`, run `node bin/recover-output.mjs <staging directory>` to restore the kept old files.
- [ ] On a leftover lock or pending file, recover serially as the diagnostics say, then retry; do not delete the files directly.
- [ ] To get back an older version after the commit point, use your own version control or backups.
